No NaN/subnormal/Inf cases where the original Apple baseline is already known wrong. Independent stored-F32 ordering/value-bit/first-index oracle checks both ports before timing. Exact generator/bytes are locked with the benchmark contract before build.

phase_ledger.phase: Context/Queue/program/slot construction and fixed input/host readback buffer allocation
phase_ledger.reason: Persistent single-step decode/batch consumer. Both arms have one independent invocation, queue/native context and stable resident input, two output ports, original workspace and native owners. Cold costs remain in P0; do not move old per-call sort work into construction.

phase_ledger.phase: Input upload and original compile/JIT/library warmup
phase_ledger.reason: Upload the exact same normal-F32 bytes once per arm; complete all uploads and cold compilation before timing. Three independent-oracle cycles and eight complete warm iterations per arm precede samples. No logits upload is hidden in one arm only.
Apple/Vulkan bind original resident input once; CPU/CUDA still pass identical borrowed input/output views at every submit. Bound payload is not preselected, repacked or cached by value.

phase_ledger.phase: Per-step public admission and native enqueue
phase_ledger.reason: CPU/CUDA OperationInvocation.submit and real QueueSequence/phase/alias checks; Apple/Vulkan Invocation.submit, original result slot and worker/native admission. No Graph Copy adapters added to this one-operation S1 comparison.

phase_ledger.phase: All selection, original full-sort work, keys, conversions and result production
phase_ledger.reason: Both output ports are computed each iteration. Original CPU fills all Entry values and partial_sorts; original CUDA builds/sorts keys+indices and extracts both outputs; original Apple stable argsort/slice/gather; original Vulkan ordinary managed/fallback lowering and full sorting. Candidate original S1 scan/reductions remain hot. All native per-call temporaries and their natural replacement/free are charged.

phase_ledger.phase: Checked completion, native retirement and result/error visibility
phase_ledger.reason: Wait through actual public Completion/OwnedResult. CPU shared submit completes inline; CUDA event synchronization/retire_slot precedes success; Apple evaluates, synchronizes stream and waits every output before done; Vulkan waits fence and retires every managed region before terminal success. No event-record-only or result-submission-only timing.

phase_ledger.phase: Read both selected values and indices to preallocated host result buffers
phase_ledger.reason: F32 values plus I32 indices, exactly8*R*K bytes. CPU BufferView reads; CUDA two actual device-resource reads; Apple native array data+memcpy after successful evaluation; Vulkan two Context.download calls including their staging allocation, command/fence waits, mapping/invalidate/copy and temporary owner destruction. No full-vocabulary D2H; no first-arm-only readback.

phase_ledger.phase: Step-local Completion, successful owned result and temporary public handle release
phase_ledger.reason: All step-local objects leave scope before the measured callback returns. Original invocation/program/context owners remain alive. No abandoned completion, cancellation retention or external callback owner is used in these success-only S1 rows.

phase_ledger.phase: Prior retained native result replacement / worker tail in steady replay
phase_ledger.reason: Apple clears prior arrays at each submit and the single runtime worker cannot execute the next job until the prior admitted reference tail returns. Full warm cycles place this cost inside steady replay in both arms. Vulkan buffers are original invocation-owned allocations and wait observes retirement. No per-step Context close is invented.

phase_ledger.phase: Last retained result, program/workspace/invocation destruction, runtime/library/allocator caches and final Context/Queue close
phase_ledger.reason: One terminal retained native result and Apple post-done wake/deliver(empty)/worker-reference tail may outlive a step wait; the Invocation remains owned, so this tail cannot destroy it. Do not claim all host callbacks or private native caches are freed at step return. Teardown is executed after the timed block, separately recorded, and is the same persistence policy on both sides.

This is the fixed success-only S1 performance workload, not the correctness/risk domain; original ordinary and risk evidence separately cover those required journeys. No applicable unrun risk is changed to N/A here.

Both O(RV), serial rows under the original caller-thread executor, two fixed output buffers, original map/flush and Queue/Completion bookkeeping. Creation/free is cold; every old Entry fill/partial_sort and both output copies remain hot.

Full radix sorting is linear in fixed key width but performs more passes; do not describe it as comparison-sort O(VlogV).
resource_ledger.apple: Original full argsort/key and layout intermediates versus K1 integer ordered-key native arg reduction; K3 still stable argsort/slice/gather with corrected integer keys. MLX owns its allocations/fusion and private caches; all per-call native arrays are hot, final retained owner/caches are cold. Original runtime job mutex/wake/refcounts and result-slot lifetime stay on both sides.

Candidate uses two bounded pair-reduction dispatches and8*R*ceil(V/4096) scratch bytes:488B at R1 and7808B at R16. Original queue mutex/fence/managed-retirement overhead is charged; both selected-output download staging allocations and native command/fence/memcpy teardown are charged. Driver/private pools remain separately unknown.
resource_ledger.common: Same persistent input/output descriptors/owners and public framework. Record actual provider/implementation/runtime properties, declared workspace/persistent/private bytes, native output arity and exact readback bytes. No shared-atomic/lock/wake/syscall count or allocator-zero promise is inferred from a timer. Source anchors define where those existing operations occur.
